decisions.difference: A: (clinical_finding "Clinical finding") root  vs  B: or of 15 common symptoms + active Fever (red-box check_for task)
decisions.reason: The box reads "Give urgent attention to the patient with any of" with no complaint; the root concept asks every patient with anything recorded, while B's list skips patients whose complaint is not a common symptom.

decisions.difference: A: (active_condition Diabetes mellitus)  vs  B: also (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Diabetes mellitus" "disorder") (qualifier (snomed_concept "Known present" "qualifier value"))) (glucose measure task)
decisions.reason: "known diabetic" is a known chronic condition; Will's briefing pairs the Known present form in check_for with active_condition in due_to, and B's or-form accepts both.

decisions.difference: A: Cough or Difficulty breathing  vs  B: also Dyspnea (RR/SpO2 measure task)
decisions.reason: "If coughing/difficulty breathing": Dyspnea is the recorded common-symptom form of difficulty breathing and Difficulty breathing is not its descendant, so both are needed to cover the page's words.

decisions.difference: A only: (active_condition Pregnancy) for the booking-visit measure task
decisions.reason: "Patient is pregnant": kept A's task but used the clinical_finding form, as for every other Pregnancy condition, because no rule diagnoses Pregnancy at probable.

decisions.difference: A only: (active_condition Hypertensive disorder, systemic arterial) for the hypertension measure task
decisions.reason: "Patient has hypertension" is the branch's condition, so it comes from the patient's record; the task itself is unsettled (see measured).

decisions.difference: A only: (active_condition Diabetes mellitus) for the diabetes measure task
decisions.reason: "Patient has diabetes": the same known-diabetes or-form as the glucose task, so a diabetic recorded on the red-box questions also gets the branch checks.

decisions.difference: A: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Alleged victim of sexual assault" "situation") (qualifier (snomed_concept "Recent" "qualifier value")))  vs  B: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Victim of sexual aggression" "finding") (qualifier (snomed_concept "Recent" "qualifier value")))
decisions.reason: "Recent sexual assault" does not say alleged; Victim of sexual aggression carries the synonym "sexual assault" and is the general international concept.
The management line says "known diabetic"; asking it lets the glucose task fire and follows Will's known-chronic-condition form.
"If coughing/difficulty breathing, also check respiratory rate and oxygen saturation": with A's root trigger Cough can be asked; it feeds the measure task.

decisions.difference: A only: Headache, Finding of vomiting
decisions.reason: "Headache and vomiting" is a red-box item; B left these out only because they were in its own trigger list, which the final build does not use.

decisions.difference: A only: Purpuric rash (A and B both have Non-blanching rash)
decisions.reason: "Purple/red rash that does not disappear with gentle pressure" describes a purpuric rash as well as a non-blanching one; the two are unrelated in SNOMED, so both are listed.

decisions.difference: Qualifier order on Muscle weakness / Numbness / Visual disturbance: A (Sudden onset, Recent) vs B (Recent, Sudden onset)
decisions.reason: "Recent sudden onset": both builds use the same concepts and both qualifiers; qualifier order has no effect on matching, so A's text was kept.

decisions.difference: A: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Alleged victim of sexual assault" "situation") (qualifier (snomed_concept "Recent" "qualifier value")))  vs  B: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Victim of sexual aggression" "finding") (qualifier (snomed_concept "Recent" "qualifier value")))
decisions.reason: Same as the check_for decision: the page says "Recent sexual assault", not alleged.
Same as the check_for decision: the page's "purple" rash that does not blanch is a purpuric rash.

decisions.difference: Qualifier order on Muscle weakness / Numbness / Visual disturbance (A vs B)
A only: 3 branch measure tasks (pregnant: MUAC, height; hypertension: height, waist circumference, glucose; diabetes: glucose, height, waist and hip circumference)  vs  B: none
decisions.final_expr: MUAC, Body height, Waist circumference, Hip circumference, Blood glucose status
decisions.reason: The page lists these as checks ("Check at booking visit", "Check at every visit", "Check once a year"), so A's encoding is closer to its words; but visit frequency can't be expressed, so they fire more often than the page intends (B's reason for leaving them out).

notes: Both builds passed. A was taken as base because of its every-patient trigger and its encoding of the three branch boxes. Seven conditions were taken from B or changed: the sexual-assault concept, the known-diabetes form (check_for plus the glucose and diabetes-task triggers), Dyspnea in the RR/SpO2 trigger, and Pregnancy in clinical_finding form for the booking-visit task. Neither build encoded the 'seen promptly' vital-sign box (there's no priority below Urgent); that is kept as Could not model. The diff counts three qualifier-order differences in check_for and three in priority_condition; they are equivalent and are recorded as one decision per role.
